editor.centroCellaNota: It writes half the cell into the two fields — right now {0} and {1} — which is the point almost every hatch rotates around. For a different centre, such as a corner of the cell, type the values by hand.
campo.comandoNota: SVG commands: M/m move, L/l line, H/h V/v horizontal/vertical line, C/c S/s Q/q T/t curves, A/a arc, Z/z closes. Upper case = absolute coordinates, lower case = relative to the previous point.
campo.poligonoNota: The outline closes by itself between the last vertex and the first, so the figure has an inside that can be filled. At least {0} vertices are needed.
campo.spezzataNota: The polyline stays open: the last vertex is not joined back to the first. Filling is possible but rarely wanted, which is why it is off by default. At least {0} vertices are needed.
campo.sorgenteNota: An uploaded file is embedded in the pattern as a data URI: the downloaded SVG stays complete outside the application too, but the saved document grows accordingly. An http/https address keeps the pattern light and depends on the resource staying reachable.
campo.immagineSegnaposto: Placeholder: choose a file or paste an address.
campo.immagineCollegata: Image linked from an external address.
campo.immagineNonImmagine: The selected file is not an image ({0}).
campo.immagineTroppoGrande: The file is over the {0} MB limit ({1} kB).
campo.lineaDiBaseNota: Y is the baseline of the text, not its top edge: the letters sit above that level.
campo.carattereNota: The font is not embedded in the SVG: it is a reference to what is installed on whoever opens it. Giving a fallback family (Segoe UI, sans-serif) keeps the text readable everywhere.

filtro.rimuoviTitolo: Removes the filter and all its steps
filtro.premessa: A filter changes the look and colour of the whole drawing in one go, without touching the elements. It applies to the painted surface and not to the single tile: a blur crosses the joins instead of leaving a seam there.
filtro.rimetti: Put this step back to work
filtro.feColorMatrix.nota: Saturation, hue, greyscale, or the twenty coefficients written by hand.
filtro.feComponentTransfer.nota: Brightness, contrast, gamma, inversion: one curve per channel.
filtro.feGaussianBlur.nota: Softens. It is the step used most often, and the one that spills furthest.
filtro.feDropShadow.nota: A drop shadow, with direction, softness and colour.
filtro.feMorphology.nota: Thickens or thins the strokes. On a fine hatch it is the way to give it weight.
filtro.feOffset.nota: Moves, and nothing else. It earns its place inside a chain, not on its own.
filtro.feFlood.nota: Fills with a colour. On its own it covers everything: it has to be composed with something.
filtro.feTurbulence.nota: Generates veins or clouds. It is the raw material for displacement.
filtro.feDisplacementMap.nota: Moves the pixels following a second image: with noise it gives the hand-drawn stroke.
filtro.feConvolveMatrix.nota: Sharpening, embossing, outlines: every pixel becomes a weighted average of its neighbours.
filtro.feBlend.nota: Blends two images with the modes of photo editing: multiply, screen, overlay…
filtro.feComposite.nota: Combines two images: over, in, out, or metered one by one.
filtro.feMerge.nota: Stacks several results, the first at the bottom. It is how the drawing goes back on top of its shadow.
filtro.sconosciuta: unrecognised step, kept as it was
filtro.combaciaBordi: Make the noise meet at the edges
filtro.bordo.opposto: Take up from the opposite side
filtro.notaSaturazione: Zero takes all the colour away, 100% leaves it as it is, beyond that it heightens it.
filtro.notaLuminanza: The drawing becomes a mask: where it was light it disappears, where it was dark it stays. On its own it leaves a black silhouette — it goes together with a solid colour and a composite, as in the «Single hue» effect.
filtro.notaLivelli: One curve per channel. Setting R, G and B the same way gives brightness and contrast; channel A touches transparency, and raising it makes opaque even what was empty.
filtro.notaTintaPiena: On its own it covers the whole area: after it you need a composite or a blend to decide where the colour should stay.
filtro.notaRumore: Noise does not consume the previous step: it only generates. That is why it always has to be named in the «Result» field and called back from a displacement or a blend — and the drawing has to be named in turn, otherwise the step after the noise finds the noise in its hands instead of the drawing, and that is all that is left on screen.
filtro.notaDivisore: A divisor of zero means «the sum of the coefficients»: it keeps the brightness where it was.
filtro.notaLivelliPila: The layers stack from the top: the first one is at the bottom. Empty means «the result of the previous step».
filtro.notaIgnota: The step «{0}» is not handled by this version: it is kept in the document without being applied.
filtro.notaCollegamenti: Left empty, the steps chain up in the order they appear. Naming a result is only useful in order to call it back later on.
filtro.notaEffetti: The steps of the effect are added after the ones already there.
filtro.notaArea: The area is given as a percentage of the painted surface. Widen it when an effect comes out cut: a shadow offset by twenty pixels on a surface of two hundred leaves the 110% and is chopped clean off.
filtro.notaSconfina: This filter has at least one step that spills over.
filtro.notaSpazio: In linear space the sums are done on light, as is physically correct, and blurs seem to lighten. The specification defaults to that; here we start from sRGB because it is what somebody moving a slider expects to see.
filtro.notaSuperficie: The filter applies to the painted surface, not to the single tile: a blur crosses the joins instead of leaving a seam there. In the single-cell preview, which is as wide as the cell, the effects that spill over appear cut at the sides — on the real surface that does not happen.
preset.grigi.nota: Takes the colour away and leaves the tones.
preset.seppia.nota: Turns everything brown, like an old print.
preset.caldo.nota: Shifts everything towards red: terracotta, earth, wood.
preset.freddo.nota: Shifts everything towards blue: concrete, metal, glass.
preset.unica.nota: Repaints everything in one colour, keeping the tones.
preset.piuContrasto.nota: Pushes the lights away from the darks.
preset.menoContrasto.nota: Brings the tones together: the drawing settles into the background.
preset.schiarisci.nota: Raises every tone without touching the colour.
preset.sbiadito.nota: Lighter and flatter all round: a hatch meant to sit under something else.
preset.biancoNero.nota: Two tones only, no greys. It survives the photocopier and black-and-white printing.
preset.pochiToni.nota: Cuts each channel down to five steps: the look of screen printing.
preset.marcato.nota: Thickens the lines: a thin hatch stops disappearing in print.
preset.sottile.nota: Thins the lines: a hatch that was too dense can breathe again.
preset.nitidezza.nota: Accentuates the edges. Go gently: past a point it starts to halo.
preset.contorni.nota: Keeps only the edges and drops the fills: the drawing becomes an outline.
preset.rilievo.nota: Lights from the left and shades to the right: the motif looks engraved.
preset.ombraMorbida.nota: Lifts the motif off the background with the faintest shadow.
preset.alone.nota: A coloured glow around the shapes, the drawing on top untouched.
preset.sfocato.nota: Softens everything. Useful for a background that must not be read.
preset.aMano.nota: Breaks the edges up with noise: the lines stop looking machine-drawn.
preset.smerigliato.nota: Like looking through ribbed glass: it ripples and softens.
preset.invecchiata.nota: Brown tones and an uneven grain: four steps, every one of them editable.
